properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. When a plan moves during execution — "the motorcade slips thirty minutes" — somebody has to be told, and the question is who decides that. (a) SUBSCRIPTION, the way every coordination tool works: you join a channel, or somebody remembers to include you on the distribution. Cheap, familiar, and it fails one way every time — the person who most needed to know was not on the list, and nobody finds out until it matters. (b) DERIVED FROM THE BLAST RADIUS: propagate_from already returns who a change impacts, including which published boundaries it crosses, so the owners of the impacted regions ARE the distribution. Nobody maintains a list, nobody is spammed with changes that cannot touch them, and when the plan changes shape the distribution changes with it for free. (c) BOTH — derived by default, with an explicit watch for people who want a region they do not own. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO (b), recorded beside it: a blast radius is only as good as the edges that exist, so an unrecorded dependency means a silent non-notification — which is the same failure as (a), reached by a different route, and arguably harder to notice because the mechanism looks principled. The mitigation is that a missing edge is already what detect_gaps hunts, so the honesty debt has an owner.
properties.name: OPEN — is notification computed from the blast radius, or subscribed to?
properties.rationale: This is the most distinctive idea in the 1000-planner exploration and the strongest reason reflow2 would belong in that problem rather than a chat tool with a plan attached: a FRAGO is a ChangeEvent whose blast radius is computed, and "who does this break" is a question reflow2 already answers. It is the same shape as every other answer in this project — computed, not remembered — and it inherits the honesty rules, so a notification would have to say what changed, what it impacts and what is now unresolved, never "the plan was updated". Kept separate from dec:live-tier because the mechanism choice is separable: (b) is worth building for a single team on the repo-file architecture, with no hosting at all, the moment anyone wants it.
